title: The corner pictures
note: The plate, the car and the eye: three photographs graded to one paper stock and cut to a ladder of WebP under portfolio/img/ - and, for the plate and the eye, a third ladder that is the Moonlight's light on the picture. The Kernel's corners.ts picks a rung at run time, so a re-bake shows on the page as soon as this tree is rebuilt.
needs: the original frame. The raws are gitignored, so `source` has to point at your own copy; without one the run stops on `no such file` and nothing is written.

groups.name: What is being baked
groups.note: One picture per run. build-plate.py names every file it writes after the picture's stem, and clears anything under that stem this run did not write.

params.label: the frame
params.note: The original photograph, which is NOT in this repository - see the recipe's `needs`. A relative path is read from the repository root.

params.label: which picture
params.note: The plate is bottom-left, the car top-right and the eye bottom-right. Each has its own two grades below, because a picture on black wants its own endpoints rather than more of light's - and the plate and the eye a third, the Moonlight's light on them, with the light's own numbers beside it.

groups.name: Grade - the plate, light
groups.note: build-plate.py's PLATE_LIGHT, stage by stage. It is baked into the WebP, so nothing here moves the page until this Bake has run.

params.label: exposure %ile
params.note: Which percentile of the building's brightness is driven to the exposure below. High enough to mean the sunlit stone; short of 100 so one specular highlight cannot set the whole frame.

params.label: exposure
params.note: Where that percentile lands, in linear light, before any tone curve. This is the brightness knob; everything below shapes what it hands over.

params.label: colour kept
params.note: Fraction of the original chroma left in. 0 is a duotone and the endpoints are then the only colour in the picture; 1 keeps the day as it was.

params.label: contrast
params.note: How far the tone curve is blended toward a smoothstep S. 0 leaves it straight.

params.label: highlight push
params.note: Lifts the top of the range without clipping it - a power of the INVERSE, so it cannot take anything past white. 1 is off.

params.label: blacks land on
params.note: Where black ends up. Lifting it off #000 is what stops the plate reading as a photograph and starts it reading as stock.

params.label: whites land on
params.note: Where white ends up. A hair above the paper and the sunlit stone stays the brightest thing in the corner without glowing.

params.label: grain
params.note: Monochrome, weighted to the mids: none in the lifted blacks, where it would read as sensor noise, and none in the highlights, where it would read as JPEG.

groups.name: Moonlight - the plate
groups.note: The third ladder, plate-moonlit-<width>.webp: the Moonlight's light ON the plate, which src/kernel/corners.css screens over the dark page and breathes with the sky. A grade and then a light - build-plate.py, THE MOONLIT LADDER and relight(). The moon stands high and to the right of this corner.

params.label: exposure %ile
params.note: Which percentile of the building's brightness is driven to the exposure below. The same stage as the other two grades, on the same frame.

params.label: exposure
params.note: Where that percentile lands, in linear light, before any tone curve.

params.label: colour kept
params.note: Fraction of the original chroma left in - and this block alone may go past 1, which is MORE colour than the day had: the 'ever so slightly more colourful' a warm stone reads as under a cool light, put into the file rather than hoped for from the blend.

params.label: contrast
params.note: How far the tone curve is blended toward a smoothstep S. A little more than the ghost under it, because a light finds edges.

params.label: highlight push
params.note: Lifts the top of the range without clipping it. 1 is off.

params.label: blacks land on
params.note: Black, and it is the meaning of the ladder rather than a choice: this layer is SCREENED over the page, and a screened black is transparent. An unlit pixel adds nothing. Lift it and the whole picture glows.

params.label: whites land on
params.note: THE LIGHT'S COLOUR - where fully lit white stone lands, so the moon on limestone: a cool pale blue. The sky glow in kernel-moonlight is the darker end of the same light. This is also the colour of the glint below.

params.label: grain
params.note: Monochrome, weighted to the mids, the same stream as the other two ladders so the theme flip moves no grain.

params.label: light from - azimuth, elevation
params.note: Where the moon is, as seen from this picture, in degrees: azimuth 0 is from the right and 90 from straight above; elevation 0 is grazing along the picture and 90 is straight down the reader's line of sight, which lights everything alike and shades nothing. Two numbers in one control because it is one direction.

params.label: relief - strength, radius
params.note: The fine bump: the picture's own luma read as height, smoothed by this radius in SOURCE pixels, and tilted by this strength. This is the ribs of the dome and the members of the lattice catching the light on the side that faces it. 0 strength is off.

params.label: form - strength, radius
params.note: The coarse bump, at a radius a hundred times the relief's: the whole curve of the dome rather than its ribs. The day's shading is a rough guide to form and a fair one to relief, so this is kept gentler than that. 0 strength is off.

params.label: glint - strength, shininess
params.note: Blinn-Phong: how bright a face turned squarely between the moon and the reader flares, and how narrow that flare is. It is the light's colour, not the stone's.

params.label: wrap
params.note: How far the light reaches round a face turned away from it. 0 is Lambert, and a bump's far side falls to black; a little wrap keeps the shadow side of a rib in the picture.

groups.name: Moonlight - the eye
groups.note: The eye's moonlit ladder, the same way. The moon stands nearly over this corner, so the light comes down the mast rather than across it, and the lattice is finer than the dome's ribs.

groups.name: The sky matte
groups.note: No sky is wanted, only the building - the page's own paper is the sky. Hysteresis, as in a Canny edge: the confident pixels vouch for the marginal ones they touch. Not per theme and not per picture: it is the shape of the building, which is one photograph either way.

params.label: bright seed
params.note: How bright a pixel must be to START a patch of sky. This is the confident test.

params.label: dim spread
params.note: How bright it must be to STAY in one it already touches. The result is insensitive to where this is put anywhere on the plateau from 0.085 down to 0.065.

params.label: edge softness
params.note: Blur on the alpha, in output pixels, so the roofline does not stair-step. Only a matte this script CUT needs it; a supplied one arrives anti-aliased already.
